newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates stable on returning funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates stable on returning funds.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates sank at mid-session on Monday as payments returning to the banking system replenished liquidity despite a continuing exodus of funds into the red-hot stock market, dealers said.

At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 6.972 percent against Saturday's 6.888 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 6.50-6.65 percent against 6.50-6.75.
The stock market, furthering a long-running bull charge on huge turnover, closed 0.87 percent higher on Monday at 9,833.77, the index's highest closing level since April 12, 1990.
Turnover was voluminous at T$232 billion.
The central bank planned to continue recent mop-up measures on Monday, announcing an issue of T$11 billion negotiable certificates of deposit.
Dealers said that despite the central bank's move and big cash demand in the stock market, the money market drew enough liquidity from returning payments to enable rates to stabilise.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9725-5.9730 percent against 5.9700.
